Hannahville Indian Community

Hannahville has its own Potawatomi community history in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. Its account follows families who resisted removal, lived among related communities and returned toward the Cedar River area. It also records later efforts to build community infrastructure. The page combines institutional narrative, an attributed1964 missionary biography and a milestone list. These voices do not always agree on dates, so this guide preserves that uncertainty rather than assigning a definitive founding or recognition year.

Peter Marksman — historical missionary context
Photographer not identified · In John H. Pitezel, Life of Rev. Peter Marksman · Drew University/GCAH via Internet Archive · Public-domain historical U.S. publication

Source & image record ↗ · Public-domain historical U.S. printed portrait — pre-1923 publication basis

The complete535×857 available book-reader preview retains the printed Rev. Peter Marksman caption. Hannahville’s own history connects this Ojibwe Methodist missionary with its settlement history; this is not a portrait of a Potawatomi government, a present member or all Hannahville families. The volume is an outside missionary account whose interpretations are not endorsed. Internet Archive catalogues it as1911; call number and handwritten title-page date indicate1901. Exact edition and original portrait photographer/date remain unresolved, while both recorded publication dates precede1923. Only the available preview, catalogue, title/frontispiece and selected opening text were inspected; no full-volume reading or high-resolution original inspection is claimed. Reuse relies on the historical U.S. publication, not an invented Internet Archive license. Exact available full-frame JPEG copied unchanged; CSS crops and overlays affect card/backdrop display only.

Community continuity and records

Hannahville History ↗

Community-published accounts of removal resistance, settlement and twentieth-century infrastructure. The page combines several voices and chronologies; its recognition dates conflict internally.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope
